basics.name: Dr Jared Jeyaretnam
basics.summary: I am a Research Fellow at the University of Nottingham, where I work on non-equilbrium quantum-many body dynamics, with a particular interest in circuit-based approaches. I previously completed my PhD at University College London before undertaking a postdoc at the University of Leeds.

work.summary: Jointly supervised by Adam Gammon-Smith, Juan P. Garrahan, Bruno Bertini, and Igor Lesanovsky. I work on non-equilbrium quantum-many body dynamics, with a particular interest in quantum information, tensor networks, and quantum circuits.

Working with Zlatko Papic and the Theory Group, I researched ergodicity-breaking phenomena such as Hilbert space fragmentation in lattice gauge theories and many-body localisation, using diverse numerical techniques such as exact diagonalisation, tensor networks, perturbation theory, Clifford circuits, and the real-space renormalisation group.

publications.name: Quantum trajectory simulation of two-dimensional non-equilibrium steady states with a trapped ion quantum processor
publications.summary: We experimentally realise quantum trajectories for a two-dimensional system—of hard-core bosons or fermions—driven by stochastic particle injection and removal at opposite corners of a square lattice. We probe the resulting non-equilibrium steady state and persistent current, finding measurable effects from particle statistics, interactions, and an applied magnetic field, showcasing both the power and current limitations of quantum computers as a platform for studying open quantum many-body systems.

publications.name: Ergodicity breaking in matrix-product-state effective Hamiltonians
publications.summary: We demonstrate that the DMRG effective Hamiltonian—an object routinely used to variationally approximate ground states—encodes detailed information about thermalization dynamics far from equilibrium. In the random-field XXZ spin chain, its spectrum captures the thermal-to-many-body-localised transition, including spatially-resolved probes of ergodic bubbles, as well as quantum many-body scars, establishing it as a versatile spectral probe of ergodicity breaking in large systems beyond the reach of exact diagonalisation.

publications.name: Hilbert space fragmentation at the origin of disorder-free localization in the lattice Schwinger model
publications.summary: Recent works have reported potential disorder-free localization in the lattice Schwinger model. Using degenerate perturbation theory and numerical simulations based on matrix product states, we identify the origin of a claimed ultraslow growth of entanglement as due to an approximate Hilbert space fragmentation and an emergent dynamical constraint on particle hopping

publications.name: Renormalisation view on resonance proliferation between many-body localised phases
publications.summary: We study the statistical properties of many-body resonances in a disordered interacting Ising chain - which can host symmetry protected topological order - using a Clifford circuit encoding of the real space renormalisation group. We show that both MBL phases present remain stable to resonances, but in the vicinity of the transition between them localisation is destabilised by resonance proliferation.

publications.name: Quantum scars and bulk coherence in a symmetry-protected topological phase
publications.summary: Quantum many-body scars provide a novel mechanism for enhancing coherence of weakly entangled states; while coherent edge modes in certain symmetry protected topological (SPT) phases can persist away from the ground state. We uncover many-body scars and their implications on bulk coherence in such an SPT phase, shedding light on their role in preserving SPT order at finite temperature and the possibility of coherent bulk dynamics in models with SPT order beyond long-lived edge modes.
